newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish drugmakers see exports doubling over 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Danish drugmakers see exports doubling over 5 yrs.

text.p: Danish drug exports are expected to double in value over the next five years, despite falling prices on the international market, the national manufacturers' organisation said on Tuesday.

"We expect 1996 exports to be around 14 billion crowns. In the year 2002 we estimate that the figure will be at least doubled, despite stiffer competition," Poul Erik Pyndt, head of the Association of Danish Pharmaceutical Industry, told Reuters.
He said the 1996 export total represented annual growth of around eight percent, down from 1995's 19 percent, but he saw double-digit growth returning in subsequent years.
Pyndt added that the forecast could be altered if a Danish firm came up with a single new product breakthrough.
But he said that a dearth of new science graduates in Denmark meant that Danish companies might have to move more of their research activities abroad.
Novo Nordisk director Ulrik Lassen agreed:
"It is already difficult to get enough qualified Danish researchers and we fear that it will be worse in the coming year," he told Reuters.
Novo is the world's biggest manufacturer of insulin and rated 195 on the Financial Times list of the top 500 European companies.
